ai.literal: Having seen, having heard, having tasted, having smelled, having touched, which knows, all five senses, with the bright-braceleted woman, they exist.
ai.translation: The delights of all five senses—sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch—are found together in this woman with bright bracelets.
ai.modern: கண்டு, கேட்டு, உண்டு, முகர்ந்து, தொட்டு அறியப்படுகின்ற ஐந்து புலன்களின் இன்பங்களும் இந்த ஒளிமிக்க வளையல்களை அணிந்த பெண்ணிடமே ஒருங்கே உள்ளன.
ai.explanation: The poet describes the completeness of the lover's embrace. While the five senses usually find pleasure in five different things, here all five sensory delights are experienced at once in the presence of the beloved. The word 'ஒண்தொடி' (bright bracelet) is used as a metonymy for the beautiful woman herself, emphasizing her allure.

ai.literal: For disease, medicine (is) other things indeed; beautifully jeweled woman, for her affliction, she herself (is) medicine.
ai.translation: For ordinary diseases, the cures are found in other things. But for the affliction caused by this beautifully jeweled woman, she herself is the only cure.
ai.modern: சாதாரண நோய்களுக்கு மருந்துகள் வேறு பொருள்களாக இருக்கும். ஆனால் அழகிய அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த இந்தப் பெண்ணால் ஏற்படும் காம நோய்க்கு, அவளே மருந்தாக இருக்கிறாள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts ordinary physical illnesses with the affliction of love. For a normal disease (பிணி), the remedy comes from external sources like herbs or roots. However, for the lovesickness (நோய்) caused by the beautifully adorned woman, she alone is the cure. The repetition of the word 'medicine' (மருந்து) highlights the paradox that the one who causes the suffering is also the only one who can heal it.

ai.literal: the one they love - soft shoulder - than sleeping - is it sweeter - lotus - he who has eyes - world
ai.translation: Is the world of the lotus-eyed god sweeter than sleeping on the soft shoulders of the one they love?
ai.modern: தாம் விரும்பும் காதலியின் மென்மையான தோள்களில் சாய்ந்து தூங்குவதை விட, தாமரைக் கண்ணனாகிய கடவுளின் உலகம் இனிமையானதோ?
ai.explanation: The speaker asks a rhetorical question comparing the joys of love to the ultimate spiritual reward. He wonders if the heavenly world of the lotus-eyed god could possibly be sweeter than resting on the soft shoulders of his beloved. The word 'கொல்' is an interrogative particle that implies doubt, showing he believes nothing can surpass the joy of his lover's embrace. The phrase 'தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு' refers to a divine paradise, emphasizing the supreme value he places on earthly love.

ai.literal: If moving away, it burns; when approaching, it is cool; fire, where did she obtain, this woman?
ai.translation: When I move away, it burns; when I draw near, it cools. Where did this woman get such a strange fire?
ai.modern: நான் விலகிச் சென்றால் சுடுகிறது; நெருங்கி வந்தால் குளிர்கிறது. இத்தகைய விந்தையான நெருப்பை இவள் எங்கே பெற்றாள்?
ai.explanation: The lover marvels at the unique nature of his beloved's embrace. Ordinary fire burns when one gets close and loses its heat when one moves away. However, the fire of love he feels from her does the exact opposite: it scorches him with longing when they are apart, but cools and comforts him when they are together. He playfully wonders where she found such a paradoxical fire.

The word 'அமிழ்து' (ambrosia) perfectly captures this idea of a substance that grants endless life and joy.

ai.literal: In one's own home having stayed, having shared and eaten one's own things, it is like that indeed, the beautiful dark woman's embrace.
ai.translation: The embrace of this beautiful, dark woman brings a joy as sweet as staying in one's own home and sharing one's food with others.
ai.modern: தமது சொந்த வீட்டில் தங்கியிருந்து, தமது உணவை மற்றவர்களுடன் பகிர்ந்து உண்பதால் வரும் இன்பத்தைப் போன்றது, அழகிய மாமை நிறம் கொண்ட இந்தப் பெண்ணின் தழுவல்.
ai.explanation: The poet compares the joy of a romantic embrace to the profound satisfaction of hospitality. Staying in one's own home and sharing one's food with guests is considered one of the highest virtues and joys in classical Tamil culture. By equating the embrace of the beautiful woman to this specific joy, the couplet highlights that love provides a deep, fulfilling, and righteous happiness. The word 'பாத்து' is a poetic alteration of 'பகுத்து', meaning to divide and share.

ai.explanation: This couplet describes the intensity and closeness of the lovers' embrace. The word 'வீழும்' means desiring or loving, referring to the deep affection between the two. The poet emphasizes that for such deeply connected lovers, this absolute physical closeness is profoundly sweet ('இனிதே').

ai.literal: Feigning anger, understanding, uniting - these (are) love united ones obtained fruit.
ai.translation: Feigning anger, resolving it, and uniting in embrace: these are the fruits obtained by lovers who have come together.
ai.modern: ஊடல் கொள்ளுதல், பின் அதனை உணர்ந்து தெளிதல், அதன்பின் கூடி மகிழ்தல் ஆகிய இவையே காதலில் ஒன்றுபட்டவர்கள் பெற்ற பயன்களாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three stages of romantic bliss. First is 'ūṭal', the lovers' quarrel or feigned anger, which adds spice to the relationship. Next is 'uṇartal', the mutual understanding and resolution of the conflict. Finally comes 'puṇartal', the joyful reunion and physical embrace. The poet declares that experiencing these three phases is the true reward for lovers who have united in love.

ai.literal: Every time knowing, ignorance having seen, it is like that indeed, passion, every time embracing, fine-jewel-woman with.
ai.translation: Just as learning more only reveals the vastness of one's own ignorance, passion feels entirely new every time I embrace this woman with fine jewels.
ai.modern: அறிவு வளர வளர நம் அறியாமை நமக்குத் தெரிவது போல, சிறந்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த இவளைத் தழுவும்போதெல்லாம் காமம் புதிதாகத் தோன்றுகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a striking parallel between the pursuit of knowledge and the experience of physical love. As a person learns more ('அறிதோறு'), they begin to realize the immense scale of what they still do not know ('அறியாமை'). In the exact same way, every time the lover embraces the woman ('செறிதோறும்'), he discovers new, unfathomable depths of passion ('காமம்'). The word 'சேயிழை' literally means 'red or fine jewels', but here it is used as a metonymy to refer to the beautiful woman wearing them. The comparison beautifully illustrates how true love, like true knowledge, is inexhaustible and always feels fresh.
